scenes.tts: Working muscle needs more oxygen. How does the blood know to let go of more there?
scenes.visual: Title fades. A muscle fibre contracting while a red cell passes. On screen: How does the blood know?
scenes.narration: Working muscle needs more oxygen. How does the blood know to let go of more there?

scenes.tts: Use the rule. Anything that binds one shape better shifts the mix toward that shape.
scenes.visual: Population bar with T and R; a molecule labelled ? that binds only to T outlines.
scenes.narration: Use the rule. Anything that binds one shape better shifts the mix toward that shape.

scenes.tts: Three regulators prefer T: acid, carbon dioxide, and a small molecule called B P G.
scenes.caption: Three regulators prefer T: acid (H⁺), carbon dioxide (CO₂), and a small molecule called BPG.
scenes.visual: Three icons slide toward the T side of the bar: H⁺, CO₂, 2,3-BPG.
scenes.narration: Three regulators prefer T: acid (H⁺), carbon dioxide (CO₂), and a small molecule called BPG.

scenes.tts: Its full name is two three bisphosphoglycerate. It is a small anion with about four to five negative charges.
scenes.caption: Its full name is 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate. It is a small anion with about four to five negative charges.
scenes.visual: Structure of 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate with its negative charges marked.
scenes.narration: Its full name is 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate. It is a small anion with about four to five negative charges.

scenes.tts: Red cells hold nearly one B P G for every hemoglobin.
scenes.caption: Red cells hold nearly one BPG for every hemoglobin.
scenes.visual: Inside a red cell: BPG and hemoglobin icons in roughly equal numbers.
scenes.narration: Red cells hold nearly one BPG for every hemoglobin.

scenes.tts: It wedges into a central pocket between the beta chains. That pocket is wide open only in T.
scenes.caption: It wedges into a central pocket between the β chains. That pocket is wide open only in T.
scenes.visual: BPG sits in the T-state central cavity between the β chains; in R the cavity narrows and BPG is squeezed out.
scenes.narration: It wedges into a central pocket between the β chains. That pocket is wide open only in T.

scenes.tts: Predict. Add B P G to hemoglobin. Which way does P fifty move?
scenes.caption: Predict. Add BPG to hemoglobin. Which way does P50 move?
scenes.visual: Hemoglobin curve with P50 marked at 26 torr. Question on screen: add BPG, which way does P50 move?
scenes.narration: Predict. Add BPG to hemoglobin. Which way does P50 move?

scenes.tts: Up. B P G holds the molecule in T, like a doorstop. It takes more oxygen to tip the mix, so the curve shifts right.
scenes.caption: Up. BPG holds the molecule in T, like a doorstop. It takes more oxygen to tip the mix, so the curve shifts right.
scenes.visual: Curve slides right; P50 marker moves up. A doorstop icon in the T pocket.
scenes.narration: Up. BPG holds the molecule in T, like a doorstop. It takes more oxygen to tip the mix, so the curve shifts right.

scenes.tts: Acid works through the Bohr effect. Protons add to certain groups, chiefly a histidine near the end of each beta chain.
scenes.caption: Acid works through the Bohr effect. Protons add to certain groups, chiefly a histidine near the end of each β chain.
scenes.visual: A proton lands on a histidine at the end of a β chain.
scenes.narration: Acid works through the Bohr effect. Protons add to certain groups, chiefly a histidine near the end of each β chain.

scenes.tts: Those groups can then form salt bridges that steady T. So low pH lowers oxygen affinity.
scenes.visual: The protonated histidine forms a salt bridge; the bar tips toward T. Label: low pH → lower affinity.
scenes.narration: Those groups can then form salt bridges that steady T. So low pH lowers oxygen affinity.

scenes.tts: Working muscle makes acid. The acid tips hemoglobin toward T exactly where a straining muscle needs the oxygen.
scenes.visual: pH gauge at the lungs (about 7.4) versus working muscle (lower). Blood in the muscle reads off a right-shifted copy of the whole curve.
scenes.narration: Working muscle makes acid. The acid tips hemoglobin toward T exactly where a straining muscle needs the oxygen.

scenes.tts: Carbon dioxide binds the ends of hemoglobin's chains as carbamate. Those groups form their own salt bridges that favor T.
scenes.visual: CO₂ attaches to the N-termini as carbamate; new links form; bar tips to T.
scenes.narration: Carbon dioxide binds the ends of hemoglobin's chains as carbamate. Those groups form their own salt bridges that favor T.

scenes.tts: In exercising muscle, three fast signals arrive at once: falling oxygen, falling pH, and rising carbon dioxide.
scenes.visual: Three arrows on the muscle: pO₂ down, pH down, CO₂ up.
scenes.narration: In exercising muscle, three fast signals arrive at once: falling oxygen, falling pH, and rising carbon dioxide.

scenes.tts: Does a right shift spoil loading in the lungs? Acid and carbon dioxide are high in tissue, not in the lungs.
scenes.visual: Map of the route: acid and CO₂ icons crowd the muscle end; the lung end is clear.
scenes.narration: Does a right shift spoil loading in the lungs? Acid and carbon dioxide are high in tissue, not in the lungs.

scenes.tts: So their shift happens where unloading happens.
scenes.visual: Two curves: lung blood on the normal curve, muscle blood on a right-shifted copy of the whole curve. Label: the shift applies where acid and CO₂ are high.
scenes.narration: So their shift happens where unloading happens.

scenes.tts: B P G shifts the curve everywhere. But the lung end sits on the flat top of the curve, so a modest shift costs little loading.
scenes.caption: BPG shifts the curve everywhere. But the lung end sits on the flat top of the curve, so a modest shift costs little loading.
scenes.visual: Curve with a modest right shift; at 100 torr the two curves are both near full.
scenes.narration: BPG shifts the curve everywhere. But the lung end sits on the flat top of the curve, so a modest shift costs little loading.

scenes.tts: A very large shift would start to cost loading, so more is not always better.
scenes.visual: A big right shift: now the curve sags below full at 100 torr. Label: too far costs loading.
scenes.narration: A very large shift would start to cost loading, so more is not always better.

scenes.tts: B P G is the slower dial. It rises over hours to days at high altitude, part of how you acclimatize.
scenes.caption: BPG is the slower dial. It rises over hours to days at high altitude, part of how you acclimatize.
scenes.visual: A clock spinning beside a mountain; BPG level in red cells rising.
scenes.narration: BPG is the slower dial. It rises over hours to days at high altitude, part of how you acclimatize.

scenes.tts: Fetal hemoglobin has two gamma chains in place of the two beta chains. At position one hundred forty-three, it has a serine instead of a histidine.
scenes.caption: Fetal hemoglobin has two γ chains in place of the two β chains. At position 143, it has a serine instead of a histidine.
scenes.visual: Fetal hemoglobin (α₂γ₂) beside adult (α₂β₂). Position 143 highlighted: Ser in γ, His in β.
scenes.narration: Fetal hemoglobin has two γ chains in place of the two β chains. At position 143, it has a serine instead of a histidine.

scenes.tts: So it binds B P G weakly and stays at higher oxygen affinity than the mother's hemoglobin.
scenes.caption: So it binds BPG weakly and stays at higher oxygen affinity than the mother's hemoglobin.
scenes.visual: Fetal curve sits to the left of the mother's curve.
scenes.narration: So it binds BPG weakly and stays at higher oxygen affinity than the mother's hemoglobin.

scenes.tts: That lets fetal blood pull oxygen across the placenta from the mother's blood.
scenes.visual: At the placenta, O₂ dots move from maternal red cells to fetal red cells.
scenes.narration: That lets fetal blood pull oxygen across the placenta from the mother's blood.

scenes.tts: Acid, carbon dioxide and B P G all favor T. So they shift the mix toward T where oxygen must let go.
scenes.caption: Acid, carbon dioxide and BPG all favor T. So they shift the mix toward T where oxygen must let go.
scenes.visual: End card. LINE: Acid, CO₂ and BPG favor T, so they shift the mix where oxygen must let go.
scenes.narration: Acid, carbon dioxide and BPG all favor T. So they shift the mix toward T where oxygen must let go.

scenes.visual: End card. LINE: Acid, CO₂ and BPG favor T, so they shift the mix where oxygen must let go.
